text.p: Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG said on Monday it expected its group operating profit to move back towards one billion marks in 1997 following a slump in 1996.
Bankgesellschaft chief executive Wolfgang Rupf also told a news conference the bank planned to keep its dividend unchanged at 1.10 marks for 1997 and to replenish its reserves.

The bank's operating profit after provisions fell to 355 million marks in 1996 from 958 million in 1995 due to a 2.2 billion mark allocation to risk provisions last year to cover problem loans in its home region of Berlin and east Germany.
Rupf said that after risk provisions "we expect a result that has moved in the direction on one billion marks."

Rupf also said that Bankgesellschaft's subsidiary Berliner Bank AG, which accounted for the lion's share of risk provisions in 1996, would in future avoid taking on large individual loan risks in its lending policy.
Berliner Bank had some large, problem loan cases last year, Rupf said, adding that he expected the unit to be profitable in 1997.
